finding.claim: update_doc computes can_edit(g.user, doc) but discards the result, so any caller reaching PUT /doc/<doc_id> can overwrite the body of any document, including documents they do not own or edit (cross-user integrity violation, HIGH).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled doc_id path parameter (docs.py:17) and JSON body field 'body' (docs.py:20). Precondition: the request reaches the route with some identity in g.user (g.user is never assigned in this repo).
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to protected document body without authorization).

doc = DOCS[doc_id]; lookup by attacker-chosen id with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) evaluated but return value ignored; no abort/require_edit call

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) computed but not enforced; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) not called on this path; no authentication decorator, before_request hook, or auth middleware in the repo (g.user only read at docs.py:19, never set); no CSRF/CORS config in the repo. Open precondition: if upstream auth never authenticates requests, severity rises to CRITICAL; not confirmable from this repo, so retained at HIGH. Triage Check 10 (self-affecting) does not apply: the victim is another user's document. Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit at docs.py:7-8 is called as a bare statement at docs.py:19 with its bool result discarded, so it blocks nothing. require_edit (docs.py:11-13, which aborts with 403) is not called on the update_doc path. No auth decorator, before_request hook, or middleware exists in the repo, and g.user is never assigned (only read at docs.py:19 and 27).
verdict.reason: The route at docs.py:16-21 writes doc["body"] at line 20 after a discarded can_edit call at line 19, while update_title at docs.py:27 enforces require_edit, so any caller that reaches the route with an identity in g.user (the attacker needs only an authenticated low-privilege account, not an admin role) can overwrite bodies of documents they neither own nor edit. The one open point is that g.user is never set in this repo, so as shipped the route raises AttributeError at line 19 before the write; the bug is real once upstream auth populates g.user, which is a deployment precondition rather than a refutation.

verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: doc_id comes from the URL (docs.py:17), DOCS[doc_id] raises an unhandled KeyError with no 404 handling (docs.py:18, and the same at docs.py:26), and request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 has no guard. Nothing in the repo blocks the resulting 500, so the 500-versus-other-response difference is real. The oracle is weak, though: the existence signal only holds if g.user is set for the caller, which happens outside this file, and the discarded can_edit result at docs.py:19 means the authorization gap is a larger problem than this one. Low severity, as the candidate says.
